results.title: Introducing the Needle outbound engine - Needle
results.content:
## 1. Outbound still takes five tools

Most teams still assemble outbound from a pile of products: one for lists, one for enrichment, one for LinkedIn, one for email, one to tell you what happened. Each does a slice of the job. None of them can take a sentence like “find 200 VP Ops at US B2B fintechs and start a LinkedIn sequence” and actually finish it.

Agents made that sentence possible. The missing piece was an engine they could call: source people, keep cadence honest, and send on the channels that still get a reply. Without that, the agent is stuck drafting copy you paste into someone else’s sequencer.

## 2. Agent-native [...] ## 2. Agent-native

Needle ships as an MCP server and a REST API. Connect it once and outbound becomes a tool your agent already knows how to use. You do not learn a new UI. You do not babysit a sequence builder. You stay in the session where you already plan GTM work, and the engine runs the motion.

That is the difference from an AI SDR product that wants to be the product. Needle is infrastructure for the agent you chose. When a better model or a better harness shows up next month, you keep the same engine.

## 3. The engine

# Introducing the Needle outbound engine

Introducing the Needle outbound engine

In June we launchedproactive agents for revenue teams. The idea was simple: an agent that does the work around a deal, not just reports on it. Today we are shipping the engine those agents run outbound on.

You tell your agent who you want. It finds the people, writes the message, and sends on LinkedIn, Instagram, and email. The whole loop lives in the agent you already use — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Needle in Slack. We call it theagent-native outbound engine.

### Social & Community [...] #### What needs improvement

The automation depth still feels like an area that could go further. Once Needle identifies an opportunity or rehydrates a stale deal, I’d want more of the next steps to happen without adding another manual layer.

I’d also keep an eye on token usage when premium models are involved. A multi-model approach is valuable, but at scale the economics matter just as much as the intelligence.

And like most GTM AI products, the quality of the output is going to depend heavily on source-data hygiene. If the CRM is incomplete or inconsistent, even a very good agent has less to work with.

Overall, the direction is strong. The real value will come from how well Needle turns good signals into reliable action without making the GTM stack more complicated.
